subject: Recap: Deployment mode discussion — isolation & SLOs

Subject: Recap: Deployment mode discussion — isolation & SLOs

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the Acme platform team today. Thanks for walking through your high-level goals; capture of the call below and proposed next steps.

TL;DR: Based on what you shared (high-concurrency inference, strict p99 latency targets during peak, and a desire to avoid cross-tenant performance variability), Dedicated capacity or Private VPC are the two deployment modes that will give you the isolation and SLAs you want. Hosted API can be a good initial path for quick testing but is less suitable for predictable p99 at scale.

Call notes:
- Use case: real-time customer-facing features + nightly batch jobs for embeddings.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~200 QPS, peak ~1,200 QPS (bursting up to ~2k for short windows).
- Typical request: 512 tokens input, ~256 tokens output on average.
- Requirements: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms (interactive peak), strict noisy-neighbor concerns, and SOC2 + data residency for EU customers.
- Security: will need VPC peering and KMS integration for key management.

Key qualification points / recommendations:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started. Good for POC and lower throughput. No tenant-level reserved GPUs, so performance can vary during cloud-level contention.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your tenant; no bin-packing with other customers at the GPU level. Provides predictable throughput, configurable autoscale policies, and an SLA (we can outline p95/p99 latency and uptime targets in the SLA doc). Good fit if you care about predictable p99 and cost control via committed capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network-level isolation, option for on-prem air-gapped deployments. Best for regulated workloads or when you need control over the entire stack (firewalls, audit). Longer lead time.

Open questions for you (helps us size the Dedicated profile):
1) Of the peak 1.2k QPS, how much is sustained vs short bursts (seconds vs minutes)?
2) What percent of requests hit the longer 1K+ token paths?
3) Any strict blackout windows / maintenance constraints?

Next steps:
- I attached our initial Dedicated pricing and a draft SLA for you to review (RWI-dedicated-pricing.pdf, SLA-draft.docx).
- Can we schedule a 45-min infra deep-dive with your platform team and our solutions engineer (Marissa) next week? She can map Dedicated sizing to your concurrency + token distribution and go over isolation guarantees.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed set of times.

Best,

Hi Alex — great questions. See answers below; happy to go deeper on the infra call.

Q1 — physical isolation / bin-packing:
- Dedicated capacity provides tenant-reserved GPU pools. We do not bin-pack multiple tenants onto the same GPU devices in Dedicated mode. Allocation is at the pod/node pool level depending on your commit (e.g., you reserve N GPU nodes); those nodes are dedicated to your tenancy. This removes cross-tenant scheduling interference at the GPU level.

Q2 — noisy-neighbor detection & mitigation:
- Telemetry: we expose per-tenant telemetry (CPU/GPU utilization, NVMe IO, network bandwidth, request-level latency histograms) in the Console and via our metrics API.
- Detection: runtime monitors unusual tail-latency deltas vs baseline and correlates with infra signals (IO waits, GPU saturation).
- Mitigation: for Dedicated, because resources are reserved, most noisy-neighbor sources are removed. For Hosted, we apply prioritized scheduling, preemption-safe QoS for production traffic, and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants if an anomalous event affects latency.
- Historical incidents: we maintain an incident log and can provide a redacted history of noisy-neighbor events on request for enterprise evals.

Q3 — SLOs & credits:
- Dedicated (reserved pools): we offer a production SLA that covers uptime and latency windows. Typical contractual SLO we propose for Dedicated customers is 99.9% availability and a p95 latency SLA; p99 latency targets are in the SLA appendix and tied to committed concurrency (we document expected p99 windows per sizing profile). If we miss the SLA, credits are applied to the invoice in line with the SLA schedule in the draft doc I attached.
- Hosted API: best-effort latency with published regional performance profiles; no guaranteed p99 in the standard self-serve plan.

Q4 — KV cache persistence and autoscale:
- We persist KV caches to tiered fast-storage local to the node and use a warm cache handoff during scale-up events. In Dedicated, since you control the node pool, cache warmup times are predictable. We also support optional shared Redis-backed caching for state you want to guarantee across instances.

Next step suggestion: a 45-minute infra deep-dive. Marissa (cc’d) is our SR Solutions Engineer for Dedicated sizing — she can walk your infra folks through sizing options for 1.2k sustained / 2k burst, token distributions, and observed p99 latency curves from comparable customers.

Proposed times: Wed Mar 3 10:00-10:45 PT, Thu Mar 4 14:00-14:45 PT. What works for your team?

Best,
Naomi
